correctness.rationale: A finite internal-functional separation argument proves equality with the metric topology on every totally bounded subset. For the binary R-tree, the metric-functional boundary is classified directly as internals plus end Busemann functions; explicit radial sequences then give exact horoball limit sets and an every-point limit sequence.

originality.rationale: The source papers contain non-Hausdorff and every-point examples and a closed-convex theorem for d-weak limit sets, but targeted searches found no precompact-rigidity theorem, exact horoball realization, or every-point d-weak sequence in a proper CAT(0) tree. Searches of the current SCOPE archive found no overlapping record.

value.rationale: The result isolates escape to infinity as the only source of d-weak/metric disagreement in proper spaces, then shows that even a proper CAT(0) tree can exhibit maximal nonuniqueness. The exact horoball family provides a reusable geometric mechanism rather than a single counterexample.
